pointers.sentence: The questions that want a value for existing rows return `None` whatever the dictionary holds, as does `MigrationQuestioner.ask_unique_callable_default_addition` (`django/db/migrations/questioner.py:MigrationQuestioner`).

An autodetector made with no questioner makes a `MigrationQuestioner()` for itself (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.__init__`), and so never blocks: migrate's check for changes to the models that are in no migration (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.handle`) is made with one ([The migrate command, showmigrations and sqlmigrate](../migrations/migrate.md)).

An autodetector made with no questioner makes a `MigrationQuestioner()` for itself (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.__init__`), and so never blocks: migrate's check for changes to the models that are in no migration (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.handle`) is made with one ([The migrate command, showmigrations and sqlmigrate](../migrations/migrate.md)).

For any other, the graph having nothing for the application, `ask_initial` looks for a migrations package with no migration in it, as the application template makes one (`django/conf/app_template/migrations/`).

`MigrationQuestioner.defaults` is read, with no for want of an entry, only where there is no module to list: the label is no installed application's, `MIGRATION_MODULES` gives `None` for it, or the import fails (`django/db/migrations/questioner.py:MigrationQuestioner.ask_initial`).

`InteractiveMigrationQuestioner` writes its questions to `InteractiveMigrationQuestioner.prompt_output`, an `OutputWrapper` around `sys.stdout` unless it is given another, and reads each answer with `input()`, given no prompt: the answers come from standard input wherever the questions go (`django/db/migrations/questioner.py:InteractiveMigrationQuestioner.__init__`).
The word exit ends the process with status 1, not the 3 of a choice to quit (`django/db/migrations/questioner.py:InteractiveMigrationQuestioner`).

The autodetector makes the value typed the default of the operation's field and gives the operation `preserve_default=False` (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._generate_added_field`, `django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.generate_altered_fields`): a one-off default ([The field operations, and those on indexes and constraints](../migrations/field-operations.md)).

`InteractiveMigrationQuestioner.ask_unique_callable_default_addition` is a warning with two choices: a callable default will not give the rows there are unique values, since the value that fills them is made once (`docs/howto/writing-migrations.txt`), and one may go on with the migration, as the first step towards one written by hand, or quit.

`NonInteractiveMigrationQuestioner` is given, besides what its base class `MigrationQuestioner` takes, a verbosity, 1 unless told otherwise, and a function to call with a message, kept as `NonInteractiveMigrationQuestioner.log` (`django/db/migrations/questioner.py:NonInteractiveMigrationQuestioner.__init__`).

`NonInteractiveMigrationQuestioner.ask_not_null_alteration` lets the command go on: it logs, at any verbosity, and returns `NOT_PROVIDED`, on which the autodetector makes the `AlterField` with the field as the model has it (`django/db/migrations/questioner.py:NonInteractiveMigrationQuestioner`).
